title: Android Theft Protection: What to Turn On Before Your Phone Is Stolen
html:
Turn these on before your phone is lost: a screen lock, Theft Detection Lock, Offline Device Lock, Remote Lock and Find Hub. They are in Settings, then Google, then All services, then Theft protection, though not every feature exists on every phone or Android version. Also write down your phone's IMEI now, because you will need it to block a lost phone in India.

Last updated: 10 Oct 2026. Availability depends on your phone and Android version.

I looked at these settings on a vivo V23 Pro running Android 14 (Funtouch OS 14) on 11 Oct 2026. My phone has a Theft protection screen with Theft Detection Lock, Offline Device Lock and Remote Lock, and a Find Hub screen with an Allow device to be located switch. I only opened the screens for this post. Theft Detection Lock and Offline Device Lock were both off on my phone when I opened them.

First: a screen lock

Google says a screen lock must be set up before you can turn on these features. Use a PIN, pattern or password that is not easy to guess or watch someone type.

The theft protection features

  • Theft Detection Lock uses AI, the phone's motion sensors, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth to detect a sudden grab-and-run, and locks the screen automatically.
  • Offline Device Lock locks the screen after the phone goes offline, so a thief cannot cut the internet to stop you tracking it.
  • Remote Lock lets you lock the phone from android.com/lock using a verified phone number, with an optional security question.
  • Identity Check asks for biometric authentication before sensitive actions such as changing passwords or recovery details, or turning off theft protection.

To turn them on, go to Settings, then Google, then All services, then Theft protection. Google says most of these features need Android 10 or newer, some need Android 15 or newer, and they are not supported on Android Go devices, tablets or wearables.

Find Hub

Find Hub can find, lock or erase a lost phone. For it to work the phone must have power, be connected to mobile data or Wi-Fi, be signed in to a Google account, and have Find Hub turned on. Google says Find Hub turns on automatically once you add a Google account. From Find Hub you can play a sound for 5 minutes, even on silent; mark the phone as lost, which locks it; or erase it, which deletes all data permanently. If the current location cannot be found, you may still see the last known location.

On my vivo V23 Pro the Find Hub screen says: "If you lose this device or any connected Fast Pair accessories, you can use Find Hub to locate them." It has an Allow device to be located switch (on for me), a Remote Lock line ("If this device is lost or stolen, you can lock it using your phone number") and links to the Find Hub app on Google Play and Find Hub on the web. When my phone's location was off, the screen showed a warning: "Turn on device location. When location is off, you can't locate this device." I did not test Play sound or Mark as lost on a second device.

If your phone is lost or stolen in India

  1. Lock it from Find Hub or android.com/lock. Change your Google account password if you think someone can open the phone.
  2. Call your mobile operator to block the SIM, and your bank to block UPI and cards.
  3. File a police report. Sanchar Saathi's CEIR service is for blocking a lost or stolen handset across all Indian networks. The portal says you file the police report, get a duplicate SIM, and submit the blocking request with the documents it asks for.
  4. If money is taken, follow our fraud reporting steps.

Keep your IMEI somewhere other than the phone: dial *#06# to see it, or look on the box or the invoice. I dialled *#06# on my vivo V23 Pro (Android 14). It opened a screen that listed the IMEI, the ICCID and the serial number. I am not showing the numbers here.

What to do next

  1. Set a screen lock and turn on Theft protection features.
  2. Check that Find Hub is on and your location setting is available.
  3. Save your IMEI somewhere safe.
